summary: Iteration 5 — verified the two NEW backend features. 9/9 pytest cases passed in 24.8s against the preview URL. (A) GET /api/items now includes an integer pairs_count on every returned item: baseline for Aura (5 seeded pieces) is pc=4 for each (all cross-category, no formality mismatches). Verified scope isolation — David returns [] with no pc leakage. Flipping the Tops item to Washing correctly drops its own pairs_count to 0 AND reduces the total pair sum by exactly 2*baseline (i.e. every partner loses exactly 1); resetting to Ready restores identical counts. Pair rules independently reproduced on a temp profile with 8 crafted items: same-category items never pair, (Dresses,Tops) & (Dresses,Bottoms) never pair, main-garment formality must be within 1 step (Casual↔Formal =3 steps → no pair; Casual↔Business =2 → no pair; Casual↔Smart Casual =1 → pairs), and Shoes/Bags/Jewellery/Accessories pair across categories regardless of formality. Server-computed counts match a locally-rebuilt reference exactly. (B) POST /api/beauty/suggest — 401 without auth; 400 with a helpful 'Add your skin tone and undertone…' detail when the active profile has neither skin_tone nor undertone (verified on David); 200 with valid JSON containing summary (str), palette (list[str] ≥1), makeup {foundation, blush, lip, eye, tip}, hair {colour, style, tip}, avoid (list), occasion_note (str) — both with and without the optional {occasion}. Profile scoping verified by creating a fresh third profile 'TEST_BEAUTY_C' with no colouring → 400, then setting skin_tone=deep undertone=cool → 200, while David still returned 400 (no cross-profile leak). All temp artefacts cleaned up: TEST_PAIR_RULES + TEST_BEAUTY_C profiles deleted, Aura Tops item reset to Ready, 0 laundry items, only the 2 seeded profiles remain.

minor.issue: Still returns 200 on creation instead of 201 (carried over from iters 2–4).
pairs_count is computed on every list call (O(n²) rule scan). Fine for wardrobes <500 items but consider caching per user if items grow — currently OK.

action_items: None required — both new features are behaving to spec.
critical_code_review_comments: compute_pairs_counts (server.py:381-390) correctly filters by (availability or 'Ready')=='Ready' so items with a missing/None availability are still treated as Ready — matches intent, but this means an item saved without an explicit availability=Ready field still contributes to pairs. Confirmed OK by inspection.

_items_pair (server.py:364-378) skips the formality constraint when either side lacks a formality string — this is why the 5 Aura seed items (no formality set) all pair with each other. Deliberate and safe (garments without formality behave as accessories do).

GET /api/items (server.py:411-421) computes counts from ALL items but only annotates the (possibly category-filtered) sublist. This is correct: pairing math must consider the entire wardrobe even when the UI is filtered.

POST /api/beauty/suggest (server.py:1184-1216) correctly reads skin_tone/undertone from scope.profile, so X-Profile-Id switching immediately changes the AI's inputs. The 400 path fires only when BOTH are missing (using OR-not) which is user-friendly — one of the two is enough to personalise.

beauty_suggest raises 502 on AI errors and 502 when parse_json_block returns nothing. That path was not exercised in this run (no LLM outage) but the try/except around chat.send_message is present and reasonable.
BEAUTY_SYSTEM prompt (server.py:1166-1181) is well-scoped and enforces STRICT JSON with the exact keys the test asserts.

Both features are implemented correctly: pairs_count uses a clean O(n²) rule engine over the profile-scoped item list and correctly excludes laundry via the (availability or 'Ready')=='Ready' filter; beauty/suggest correctly reads the per-profile colouring block from get_scope so X-Profile-Id isolation is inherent — verified by proving David→400 remains 400 even after a sibling profile is fully configured.
